title: Lemonade Syrup / Very Berry Essence
directions: === First card: Lemonade Syrup ===
Make this syrup ahead and store in refrigerator for up to two weeks.
Peel lemon zest thinly so as not to get any of the white.
In a small saucepan stir together zest, lemon juice, water and sugar. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 3 minutes. Cool.
Strain into a bottle or jar and store in refrigerator.
Use 1-2 Tbsp. syrup per 1 cup (250 mL) water for refreshing lemonade.
Makes 20-25 servings.
=== Second card: Very Berry Essence ===
In a bowl combine berries, water and vinegar. Bruise berries by lightly pressing against side of bowl. Let stand at room temperature 8 hours, or overnight.
Strain well through a fine sieve careful not to allow pulp into the clarified juice. Measure juice.
For each 1 cup (250 mL) juice, add 1/2 cup (125 mL) sugar. Stir to dissolve.
Add 2 Tbsp. (25 mL) juice to 1 cup water or soda water for each drink.
Makes approximately 1 cup (250 mL) concentrate, enough for 10 drinks.
notes: Magazine/newspaper clipping headed 'COOL TASTES': Light and cool, key words for summer time menus. These make ahead recipes allow you to relax with the rest of the gang.

IN THE KITCHEN
with Natashya Shewchuk
Gourmet Bran Muffins
[W]ith summer nearly here, many people [li]ke to reach for something light but [w]holesome as they rush off to work or sit [o]ut in the back yard with a good book. ingredients: 1 1/2 cups ROBIN HOOD or OLD MILL Oats (375 mL)
1 cup ROBIN HOOD All Purpose Flour* (250 mL)
2 tbsp brown or granulated sugar (30 mL)
directions: MIX oats and milk in small bowl. Set aside until milk is almost absorbed, about 5 minutes.
COMBINE flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in mixing bowl. Stir well to blend.
ADD eggs and oil to oat mixture. Beat well.
ADD oat mixture to flour mixture all at once, mixing until smooth.
POUR batter by 1/4 cupfuls (50 mL) onto preheated, lightly greased griddle. Bake until fluffy and bubbles break on surface. Turn and bake other side. Serve hot with butter and/or maple syrup.

notes: A quick, easy, delicious, nutritious breakfast!

title: Golden Award White Bread
ingredients: 1/2 cup (125 mL) vegetable oil or shortening
9 1/2 - 10 1/2 cups (2375-2625 mL) Golden Award All Purpose Flour
directions: Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm water and let stand 10 minutes.
Measure warm water into a large mixing bowl; add sugar, oil and salt. Add yeast mixture and mix well. Stir in sufficient flour to make a soft, workable dough.

Turn dough out on a lightly floured surface; knead 10-15 minutes until dough is smooth and elastic. Form dough into a ball and place in greased bowl, turning once to grease the top. Cover and let rise 50 minutes or until doubled.
Punch down and shape into 4 round balls. Cover and let rest 20 minutes. Form into loaves and place in greased 1.5 L (8 1/2" x 4 1/2") loaf pans. Brush tops with oil. Cover and let rise 50-55 minutes.
Bake in 190°C (375°F) oven 35-40 minutes or until bread tests done. Remove from pans and cool on wire rack.

raw_text:
Dawn is breaking over the prairies, and though you know it's going to be a scorcher, there's still enough chill in the air to see your breath. Steamy snorts erupt from your horse's muzzle as she noses into the feedbag. Once she's been fed and watered, it's time to see what's cooking in the chuckwagon for breakfast: hotcakes and bacon for sure, and boiled coffee that would strip the shine from new leather. And if you're lucky, there's a batch of fresh hot biscuits just coming out of the cookstove - a couple of those will carry you pretty far. Maybe you can sneak a third one, if the cook's not looking...

6 cups Co-op all purpose flour

2/3 tablespoon cream of tartar
3/4 cup Co-op powdered skim milk
1 tablespoon salt
2/3 lb. 100% vegetable shortening
2 tablespoons sugar
Combine all ingredients. Mix with hands until evenly blended. Store in a sealed container in a cool place. Will keep for months.
TO MAKE BISCUITS

1 cup grated cheddar cheese (optional)
Mix ingredients together. Blend with fork until smooth. Roll out dough until it is 1" thick. Cut biscuits with an upside down glass or cup. Bake at 450° for 10 minutes. Makes 1 dozen.

title: Potato Dinner Rolls
ingredients: 1/2 cup water or reserved potato water (125 mL)
directions: Over medium heat melt butter. Add potato water and milk, heat just to lukewarm, set aside.
Put mashed potatoes and potato water mixture in a large bowl. Add the sugar, salt and eggs. Beat with a wire whisk until smooth. Add Fermipan yeast over mixture and beat again.

Add 2 cups (500 mL) of flour, beat until smooth. Mix in 3 1/2 more cups (875 mL) of flour with a wooden spoon. Gradually add the last cup (250 mL) of flour, working it in with your hands by pressing flour into dough and turning dough over, until you have a firm dough.
Cover and let rise in the same bowl for 40 minutes, or until double in bulk.

Punch dough down, place on floured surface. Sprinkle dough lightly with flour. Press dough out with fingers to a square 1 inch (2.5 cm) thick. Cut in strips lengthwise 1 1/2" (4 cm) and crosswise 1 1/2" (4 cm). Then you have 1 1/2" (4 cm) squares. If knife gets sticky when cutting just dust with flour.
Shape each square into a ball by pinching all four sides underneath to seal. Place buns almost touching in greased round or square cake pans.
Let rise covered for one hour or until doubled.
Bake in a preheated 400° F (200° C) oven for 15-20 minutes. For a soft crust brush tops with margarine or butter. Cool on racks. Makes about 40.

title: German Dark Rye Bread
directions: In a large mixing bowl pour in hot coffee. Stir in shortening, molasses and salt and continue stirring until shortening melts.
In a smaller bowl pour in lukewarm water. Sprinkle yeast over water and let stand 10 minutes. Stir with a fork and add to coffee mixture.
Beat in by hand or with an electric mixer 3 cups (750 mL) flour and 2 cups (500 mL) rye flour. Then by hand add remaining flours, working the last portion in with a rotating motion of the hand.

Turn dough onto a floured surface and knead 8 to 10 minutes. Shape into a smooth ball and place in a deep greased bowl, rotating ball to cover with grease. Cover with a damp cloth and in a warm place allow to rise 1 1/2 times original size (about 1 1/2 hours).
Punch down, shape into 3 round loaves. Roll each loaf in oat bran to garnish the top. Place on greased cookie sheets, cover and allow to rise again 1 1/2 times in volume (about 1 hour).
Bake in a 400° F (200° C) oven for 30 minutes or until hollow sounding when tapped.
notes: Printed newspaper clipping with holly decoration (Christmas issue). Intro: 'From the Purity Cookbook this round loaf is a warm accompaniment to our savory oyster stew.'

In a large mixing bowl pour in hot coffee. Stir in shortening, molasses and salt and continue stirring until shortening melts.
In a smaller bowl pour in lukewarm water. Sprinkle yeast over water and let stand 10 minutes. Stir with a fork and add to coffee mixture.
Beat in by hand or with and electric mixer 3 cups (750 mL) flour and 2 cups (500 mL) rye flour. Then by hand add remaining flours, working the last portion in with a rotating motion of the hand.
Turn dough onto a floured surface and knead 8 to 10 minutes. Shape into a smooth ball and place in a deep greased bowl, rotating ball to cover with grease. Cover with a damp cloth and in a warm place allow to rise 1 1/2 times original size (about 1 1/2 hours). Punch down, shape into 3 round loaves. Roll each loaf in oat bran to garnish the top. Place on greased cookie sheets, cover and allow to rise again 1 1/2 times in volume (about 1 hour). Bake in a 400° F (200° C) oven for 30 minutes or until hollow sounding when tapped.

directions: Crust: Mix well and line a 9-inch pie plate, save 1 tablespoon of crumbs for meringue topping. Brown for 8 minutes at 375°F.

FLAPPER PIE
Thanks to the many readers who have sent in the flapper pie recipe for Nel Kirby, the response was overwhelming. Marge Horning sends along the recipe her mother used.

Crust:
14 double graham wafers, ground fine
1/2 cup white sugar
1/4 cup melted margarine (or butter)
1 tsp. cinnamon
Mix well and line a 9-inch pie plate, save 1 tablespoon of crumbs for meringue topping. Brown for 8 minutes at 375°F.

Filling:
2 cups milk
2 egg yolks
1 tsp vanilla
2 tbsp cornstarch
1/4 cup sugar
Cook until thick. Pour hot into crust.

Meringue:
2 egg whites
3 tbsp icing sugar
1/8 tsp cream of tartar

Beat until stiff.

Pour meringue on warm pie, making sure the meringue is covering all sides of the crust so the meringue doesn't shrink. Sprinkle fine crumbs over the top. Bake at 250°F for 20 minutes, or until meringue is golden brown,

title: Bavarian Appletort Cheese Cake
directions: Cream margarine, sugar & vanilla. Blend in flour. Spread dough on the bottom & sides of 9" spring form pan.
Combine softened cream cheese & sugar & mix well. Add egg & vanilla & mix with mixer. Then pour over the pastry in pan.

Cool before removing from pan. Refrigerate.

title: Icing takes a little patience: Bakery Shop Icing / Decorator's Icing / Strawberries à la Creme
attribution: Corryine De Souza, Herald writer (Recipe Swap, Calgary Herald); Bakery Shop Icing from Betty Gladu; Decorator's Icing from Linda Homenick; Strawberries à la Creme from Chris Mulders
ingredients: === Third recipe: Strawberries à la Creme ===
8 cups strawberries, hulled, washed and thoroughly dried
directions: — Bakery Shop Icing —

Cream butter, shortening, sugar and vanilla together in a large bowl. Stir cornstarch into milk and add to sugar mixture. Beat everything at low speed until all ingredients are blended. Beat at medium speed for 5 to 7 minutes until the icing is creamy smooth and of desired consistency.
Note: This icing will appear curdled at first but don't give up. As you continue to beat it, it becomes smooth.
=== Second recipe: Decorator's Icing ===
Beat egg whites until stiff, set aside. Cream shortening, add 1/2 cup powdered sugar; cream 2 minutes. Add beaten egg whites, flavoring and remaining sugar. Cream again.
=== Third recipe: Strawberries à la Creme ===

Cut strawberries in half and sprinkle with the confectioners sugar, toss and chill for about 15 minutes. Using an electric mixer, whip the cream till stiff peaks hold their shape. Toss the Kirsch/brandy into the berries and gently fold in the whipped cream. To add the final touches, refrigerate 8 serving glasses and then dip the rims into sugar, place mixture into glasses and refrigerate at least one hour. Place a whole strawberry on the top and serve.
notes: Newspaper clipping, RECIPE SWAP column, Calgary Herald
Thanks to Betty Gladu for sending this recipe as requested by Laura MacIntosh
Linda Homenick has had this recipe for over 35 years and still uses it faithfully. This icing gives good detail. It gets crispy on the outside and stays soft inside.

raw_text:
RECIPE SWAP
Icing takes a little patience
CORRYINE DE SOUZA, Herald writer
Thanks to Betty Gladu for sending this recipe as requested by Laura MacIntosh:
Bakery Shop Icing
1/2 cup butter
6 tablespoons shortening
1 cup white sugar
2 teaspoons vanilla
1 tablespoon cornstarch
1/2 cup warm milk
Cream butter, shortening, sugar and vanilla together in a large bowl. Stir cornstarch into milk and add to sugar mixture. Beat everything at low speed until all ingredients are blended. Beat at medium speed for 5 to 7 minutes until the icing is creamy smooth and of desired consistency.
Note: This icing will appear curdled at first but don't give up. As you continue to beat it, it becomes smooth.
Here's another recipe for Laura McIntosh. Linda Homenick has had this recipe for over 35 years and still uses it faithfully. This icing gives good detail. It gets crispy on the outside and stays soft inside.
Decorator's Icing
3/4 cup of shortening
3 cups powdered sugar
2 egg whites
1/2 teaspoon flavoring
Beat eggs white until stiff, set aside. Cream shortening, add 1/2 cup powdered sugar; cream 2 minutes. Add beaten egg whites, flavoring and remaining sugar. Cream again.
This recipe is compliments of Chris Mulders. He shares this simple and elegant desert with our readers.
Strawberries à la Creme
8 cups strawberries, hulled, washed and thoroughly dried.
1-1/4 cups confectioner's sugar
1 pint heavy cream
1/2 cup Kirsch or Brandy
Cut strawberries in half and sprinkle with the confectioners sugar, toss and chill for about 15 minutes. Using an electric mixer, whip the cream till stiff peaks hold their shape. Toss the Kirsch/brandy into the berries and gently fold in the whipped cream. To add the final touches, refrigerate 8 serving glasses and then dip the rims into sugar, place mixture into glasses and refrigerate at least one hour. Place a whole strawberry on the top and serve.
Thanks to the many readers who responded to Kitty Mah's request for Amish Bread. Unfortunately, I have not recieved a starter recipe and I need it before I print the bread recipe.

■ Ken Saunders would love to find a recipe for salmon spread. It is usually served as an appetizer with crackers.

title: Turkey Stir-Fry Supreme
ingredients: 500 g (1 lb) boneless fresh Alberta turkey breast*

directions: Cut turkey into narrow strips or bite-size pieces.

Combine chicken broth and cornstarch mixture.
Add turkey and cornstarch mixture.
Stir and cook until heated through and sauce thickens.
Serve over steamed rice or noodles if desired.
notes: Use your imagination to vary ingredients and use what you have on hand.

title: Bacon - Home cured - brine
directions: gradually add the brine mixture — the potato will float when the brine solution is about 80% — which is needed in curing.
Leave bacon in crock for 15-20 days — every few days take out the meat — stir the brine — put the meat back in — submerge the meat by weighting down with a jar of water.

After curing — each piece of meat should be rinsed briefly in fresh water to remove salt, then set aside to dry. — Pat meat with paper towel, lay on wire racks (not touching) — when dry a thin clear glossy coating of dissolved protein & nutrients will cover the surface — ready to smoke.

title: Country Beef Ragout
ingredients: 2 (2) large celery stalks, cut in 1" (2.5 cm) pieces
1 (1) can (28 oz/796 ml) whole seasoned tomatoes
1 tsp. (5 ml) concentrated liquid beef stock (i.e. Bovril)
directions: 1. Brown beef cubes on all sides in lightly oiled skillet. Remove and place in oven-proof casserole.

2. In the skillet, cook onions, garlic and celery for 2 - 3 minutes and stir in remaining ingredients, except mushrooms. Bring to boil, stirring constantly. Season with salt and pepper and pour over beef.

3. Cover casserole and place in preheated 350°F (180°C) oven. After 1 hour, add mushrooms and cook for another 1-1/2 hours, removing lid for last 15 minutes. Serve over noodles or garlic mashed potatoes.

Time Saver Tip: To make this stew in a hurry, mix 1 pouch (approx. 56 g) quick stew mix with water according to package directions. Add beef and marinate in pot for 30 minutes. Bring to a boil, add remaining ingredients (using a 14 oz/398 ml) can of tomatoes instead) and simmer covered for 20 - 30 minutes.
notes: This delicious stew can also be made in the slow cooker, just combine all ingredients and cook covered for 5 - 6 hours on High, or 10 - 12 hours on Low.
Preparation time: 15 minutes. Cooking time: 2-1/2 hours. Makes 4 servings.

title: Beatrice Stuffed Mushrooms
ingredients: 1 cup chopped stems and pieces from domestic mushrooms
3 tablespoons softened cream cheese or sour cream
1/4 cup fine, dry bread crumbs, seasoned with pinch of salt and pepper
directions: 1. Clean the mushroom caps with a brush.
2. Sauté the bacon with the shallots until the bacon fat liquefies.
3. Pour off most of the bacon fat, and replace with a little of the melted butter.
4. Mix in the chopped stems and pieces, cream cheese or sour cream, bread crumbs, parsley, and salt and pepper.
5. Place the cleaned mushrooms, stem side up, on a buttered broiler pan, and fill with the mixture, heaping into rounds.
6. Drizzle a little melted butter on them, and broil until heated through and lightly browned, about 1 to 2 minutes.
LOW CALORIE RECIPE: For a lighter filling use Beatrice Light Cream Cheese and Yogurt in place of Beatrice Regular Cream Cheese and Sour Cream.

HERITAGE
BEATRICE STUFFED MUSHROOMS
12 fairly large domestic mushroom caps
2 strips bacon, chopped
1 tablespoon shallots, chopped fine
2 tablespoons melted butter
1 cup chopped stems and pieces from domestic mushrooms
3 tablespoons softened cream cheese or sour cream
1/4 cup fine, dry bread crumbs, seasoned with pinch of salt and pepper
1/4 teaspoon chopped parsley
Salt and pepper to taste
FIRST COURSES
1. Clean the mushroom caps with a brush.
2. Sauté the bacon with the shallots until the bacon fat liquefies.
3. Pour off most of the bacon fat, and replace with a little of the melted butter.
4. Mix in the chopped stems and pieces, cream cheese or sour cream, bread crumbs, parsley, and salt and pepper.
5. Place the cleaned mushrooms, stem side up, on a buttered broiler pan, and fill with the mixture, heaping into rounds.
6. Drizzle a little melted butter on them, and broil until heated through and lightly browned, about 1 to 2 minutes.
LOW CALORIE RECIPE
For a lighter filling use Beatrice Light Cream Cheese and Yogurt in place of Beatrice Regular Cream Cheese and Sour Cream.

title: Meat Sauce / Veal Cutlets
directions: — Meat Sauce —
Brown 1 lb or so of hamb. Add 1 clove garlic, S & P, 1 onion chopped, Italian seasoning – 2 Tbsp or more, 1 sm. tom. paste, 3 cans H2O, fresh or 1 can mushrooms.
Simmer for 1–2 hrs.
— Veal Cutlets —
Dip veal in flour, egg & crumbs, brown well.
Put layer sauce in pan. Put in veal. Cover veal with more sauce. Layer of Mozzarella cheese. More sauce. Sprinkle with Parmesan.
Cover with foil & Bake @ 350° 1 hr.
Serve with noodles & Caesar salad.
